model_interpretation.claim: Baseline evidence records two correct seeded cases at 1280x720 with four threads and a three-sample mean of 0.1149515407162521 seconds; no candidate comparison is available.
model_interpretation.applicability: The only measured comparison available is the correct baseline; it does not establish the effect of this threshold or culling change.
model_interpretation.next_experiment: Measure this candidate against the baseline at both requested core counts and with altered light colors, then compare the traversal savings against any increased per-pixel work.

model_interpretation.claim: Stopping subdivision when a tile has 1–3 lights should reduce recursive culling work while bounding the added per-pixel light loop to three candidates; light-count visualization retains leaf-level behavior. Skipping XY plane tests when every child fails the conservative Z tests should further reduce split work. Ceiling tile counts, clipping edge-tile depth scans, and rebuilding the tree on dimension changes preserve correctness beyond evenly divisible layouts. These are hypotheses, not measured gains.

items.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead
items.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing recursive culling and hierarchy work in MinMaxZTree, SplitTileMinMax, IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax, and traversal. In addition to tile granularity and conservative plane-test optimizations, compare stopping subdivision for tiles with small nonzero light lists against continuing to the leaves; measure saved traversal/culling against the added per-pixel light work. Preserve conservative culling, current-frame depth-bound recomputation, and correctness for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Do not add parallelism or change ShadeTileC in this branch. Validate both core counts and altered light colors.
